examples.text: Сейчас спокойно едем к тебе домой.
examples.trans: Right now we are driving calmly to your home.

examples.text: А я часа через два к тебе заеду.
examples.trans: And I will drop by your place in about two hours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вчера, когда ты в кино крепко уснула.
examples.trans: Yesterday, when you fell fast asleep at the movies.

examples.text: А я часа через два к тебе заеду.
examples.trans: And I will drop by your place in about two hours.

examples.text: А он мне заявил, что развлекаться надо вечером.
examples.trans: And he declared to me that one must have fun in the evening.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я часа через два к тебе заеду.
examples.trans: And I will drop by your place in about two hours.

examples.text: Но вы новички, мы сыграем короткий вариант, часа через два закончим.
examples.trans: But you are beginners, we will play a short version and finish in two hours.

examples.text: Через две недели.
examples.trans: In two weeks.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will drop by'.

examples.text: Надо заехать домой, принять душ, переодеться.
examples.trans: I need to stop by home, take a shower, change.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и заехать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will drop by on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Иди приведи себя дома в порядок.
examples.trans: Go get yourself ready at home.

examples.text: Ведь мы с тобой люди взрослые.
examples.trans: After all, you and I are grown-up people.

examples.text: А Елена ведёт меня на встречу с её друзьями.
examples.trans: And Elena is taking me to a meeting with her friends.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'people' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какой же ты всё-таки неблагодарный человек!
examples.trans: What an ungrateful person you are after all!

examples.text: Он хороший человек.
examples.trans: He is a good person.

examples.text: Здесь много людей.
examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'рослый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('adult / grown-up').

examples.text: Ведь мы с тобой люди взрослые.
examples.trans: After all, you and I are grown-up people.

examples.text: Он уже взрослый.
examples.trans: He's already grown up.

examples.text: Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sense, meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В смысле, у меня сегодня правда выходной?
examples.trans: Wait, do I really have a day off today?

examples.text: В смысле?
examples.trans: What do you mean?

examples.text: В этом нет смысла.
examples.trans: There's no sense in it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'really', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, у меня сегодня правда выходной?
examples.trans: Wait, do I really have a day off today?

examples.text: Это прекрасно, правда?
examples.trans: That is wonderful, isn't it?

examples.text: Слушай, может, мне и правда уволиться?
examples.trans: Listen, maybe I really should quit?

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.text: Извините, я пойду работать.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I will go work.

examples.text: Лена, ну извини, я иду, а тут наш футбол.
examples.trans: Lena, well forgive me, I was walking and here was our football.

examples.text: Извините, я тороплюсь.
examples.trans: Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: Извините, я пойду работать.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I will go work.

examples.text: Наверное, обед привезли наш, я пойду открою.
examples.trans: They probably brought our lunch, I will go open the door.

examples.text: Я сейчас пойду открою.
examples.trans: I will go open the door right now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Извините, я пойду работать.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I will go work.

examples.text: Максим, иди лучше на кухню работай.
examples.trans: Maxim, go work in the kitchen instead.

examples.text: Я и так на него работаю без выходных.
examples.trans: I already work for him without days off as it is.
